title: A task that raises Ignore shows as STARTED in event monitors
author: ChristianMurphy
body_preview: A task that raises `Ignore` sends no event after `task-started`, so Flower and other event monitors show it as STARTED for as long as they keep it. That includes the pattern from the docs where a task stores its own state and then raises `Ignore`. It has been this way since 4.0.0 and 3.1.17, and is the same on 5.4.0 and 5.5.3. title: A cold shutdown by SIGQUIT does not send worker_shutdown
author: ChristianMurphy
body_preview: A prefork worker that is stopped with SIGQUIT never sends the `worker_shutdown` signal. With `REMAP_SIGTERM=SIGQUIT` that is every stop, so a handler that flushes metrics or closes a connection there never runs. It has been this way since 4.0.0 and is the same on 5.4.0 and 5.5.3. title: A task name the worker does not have leaves its chain and chord pending and skips its errback
author: ChristianMurphy
body_preview: When a worker receives a task name it doesn't have, it stores FAILURE for that task and stops there: the errback isn't called, and the task's chain and chord stay PENDING. This happens in a rolling deploy, when a new task is called before every worker has it. It has been this way since 4.0.0 and is the same on 5.4.0 and 5.5.3. title: DynamoDB backend: pool processes race to create a missing table, and tasks that ran are stored as FAILURE
